subject: math
alignment_method: hybrid: tfidf shortlist -> grade+keyword rerank -> LLM curation (Claude Sonnet)
notes: Personal-finance spreadsheet project at HS Algebra/Modeling level. Most concrete math is in the formula objectives (net pay, percentages, sums) which map cleanly to A-SSE / N-Q / 7.RP. Several objectives are pure data entry, categorization, or reflective writing and have no math alignment. The pie-chart task lacks a clean CCSS-M anchor - MP.4 (modeling) is the strongest available fit.

objectives.title: Watch Me
objectives.description: Watch the introductory video.
objectives.note: Platform onboarding. No math standard applies.

objectives.title: Personal Information
objectives.description: Use AI to research careers and fill in personal info.
objectives.note: Career research / data entry. No math standard applies (closest ELA alignment is W.9-10.7/8 research).

objectives.title: Tax and Income
objectives.description: Use AI to research effective tax rate and income for a chosen career.

alignments.rationale: Use units to understand problems and choose units consistently - annual gross income (USD) and effective tax rate (%) must be reported with appropriate units.
Effective tax rate is a percent applied to income. Even at HS, the underlying ratio reasoning is the 7.RP percent-of-quantity skill.

objectives.title: Annual Net Pay
objectives.description: Write a formula: [Annual Gross Income] * (1 - [Effective Tax Rate]).

alignments.rationale: Interpret complicated expressions by viewing parts as a single entity - (1 - tax_rate) is the after-tax fraction acting as a single multiplier on gross income.
Interpret parts of an expression: identifying gross income, tax rate, and the subtraction-from-one structure.

objectives.title: Monthly Net Pay
objectives.description: Write a formula: annual net pay / 12.

alignments.rationale: Same compound-expression interpretation; annual_net / 12 reuses the annual-net result as a single quantity.
Unit conversion (USD/year -> USD/month) - choosing and tracking units is the core skill here.

objectives.title: Housing
objectives.description: Enter housing type and monthly cost.
objectives.note: Data entry. No math standard applies.

objectives.title: Needs List
objectives.description: List at least seven needs with notes explaining each.
objectives.note: Data entry and categorization with brief written notes. No math standard applies.

objectives.title: Sum Function
objectives.description: Use SUM() to total monthly need costs.

alignments.rationale: SUM() is a function from a domain (range of cells) to a single output value - exactly the function-mapping definition.
Use function notation and evaluate functions for inputs in their domain - SUM(C12:C26) uses spreadsheet function notation in context.

objectives.title: % Monthly Net Pay
objectives.description: Calculate percentage of monthly net pay spent on needs.

alignments.rationale: Percent-of-quantity problem - needs subtotal as a percentage of monthly net pay is exactly this 7.RP skill, even when used at HS.
Choosing units (decimal vs %) and formatting the cell as percentage.

objectives.title: Entertainment
objectives.description: Enter entertainment line-item cost.
objectives.note: Data entry. No math standard applies.

objectives.title: Wants List
objectives.description: List at least seven wants with notes.
objectives.note: Data entry and categorization. No math standard applies.

objectives.title: Reusing Formulas
objectives.description: Copy and paste cell formulas to reuse the SUM() pattern.

alignments.rationale: Look for and make use of structure - recognizing the SUM-of-range pattern transfers across the Wants subtotal.
Express regularity in repeated reasoning - same calculation structure applied to a different data range.

objectives.title: % Monthly Net Pay (Wants)
objectives.description: Calculate % of net pay spent on wants.

alignments.rationale: Percent-of-quantity, identical to the Needs % task.
Tracking units and formatting as percent.

objectives.title: Emergency Fund
objectives.description: Enter monthly emergency fund contribution.
objectives.note: Data entry. No math standard applies.

objectives.title: Financials List
objectives.description: List at least four financial goals with monthly contributions.
objectives.note: Data entry and categorization. No math standard applies.

objectives.title: Modify Copied Formulas
objectives.description: Copy, paste, and adjust cell formulas for the Financial Goals subtotal.

alignments.rationale: Look for and make use of structure - adapting the same SUM/% pattern with adjusted ranges and absolute references.
Treating the subtotal expression as a single quantity that the percent formula divides into monthly net pay.

objectives.title: % Monthly Net Pay (Financials)
objectives.description: Calculate % of net pay spent on financial goals.

alignments.rationale: Percent-of-quantity, same skill as the Needs and Wants % tasks.

objectives.title: Total Spending
objectives.description: Formula adding the three subtotals.

alignments.rationale: Interpret a sum of subtotals as a compound expression - each subtotal is itself a sum, and the total is a sum-of-sums.
Spreadsheet sum is a function over the three subtotal inputs producing one output.

objectives.title: Remaining Funds
objectives.description: Formula subtracting total spending from net pay; percent formulas for E55/E56.

alignments.rationale: [Net Pay] - [Total Spending] reads each operand as a single quantity; same compound-expression interpretation.
The accompanying percent formulas in E55/E56 are percent-of-quantity calculations.

objectives.title: Pie Chart
objectives.description: Create a pie chart visualizing the budget breakdown.

alignments.rationale: Model with mathematics - choosing a pie chart to represent categorical proportions of a budget is a modeling choice.
Use appropriate tools strategically - selecting and configuring a chart tool for the data.

objectives.note: CCSS-M does not directly anchor pie charts at HS; closest content standard would be middle-grades data display (6.SP), but Mathematical Practices are a more honest fit.

objectives.title: Notes
objectives.description: Write notes explaining at least eight budget items.

alignments.rationale: Attend to precision - explanatory notes that pin down specifics (year/make/model, sqft, etc.) tighten the model. Primary alignment is ELA writing (W.9-10.4).

objectives.note: Primarily an ELA writing task; minimal math content beyond precision-of-quantity.

objectives.title: Spreadsheet Reflection
objectives.description: Write a 25+ word reflection on spreadsheet skills learned.
objectives.note: Reflective/metacognitive writing. No math standard applies.

objectives.title: 50/30/20 Reflection
objectives.description: Write a 25+ word reflection on the 50/30/20 budgeting rule.
objectives.note: Reflective/metacognitive writing. No math standard applies.

objectives.title: AI Reflection
objectives.description: Write a 25+ word reflection on using AI in this project.
objectives.note: Reflective/metacognitive writing. No math standard applies.

objectives.title: Budget Realism (Teacher Graded)
objectives.description: Check the budget tells a believable financial story.

alignments.rationale: Interpret parameters in a function in terms of context - a 'realistic' budget is precisely about whether the parameters (incomes, costs, percentages) are sensible in context.
Model with mathematics - judging whether the model's assumptions and outputs are reasonable.

objectives.title: Reflection Quality (Teacher Graded)
objectives.description: Grade the three reflections for depth and specificity.
objectives.note: Rubric for reflective writing. No math standard applies (closest ELA alignment is W.9-10.4).

objectives.title: Accuracy and Completeness (Teacher Graded)
objectives.description: Check items are placed in the right category (Needs/Wants/Financials).

alignments.rationale: Attend to precision - correct categorization is a precision-of-classification check, but this is mostly a financial-literacy / CTE rubric.

objectives.note: Categorization rubric. Primary discipline is financial literacy / CTE rather than CCSS-M.
